lines.text: Dorothy and Burningum stare at each other.
After more than ten minutes, Dorothy begins to grow restless.
Just as she is about to speak, Burningum opens his mouth.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You were too hasty.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Inciting Nikkes and citizens to rise up toward a Third Surface Reclamation War.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Did you really think that would work?

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: All of you were dragging your feet. It was frustrating.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: So the Queen really has descended.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Yes. She has.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Then the destruction of Eden must be true as well.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: And you really are Dorothy of the Goddess Squad.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Right, I've known that all along.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: ... What?

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: I knew you were Dorothy of the Goddesses from the moment we first met.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: I knew those in the Ark regarded us as legends, but I didn't expect a Deputy Chief of all people to buy into it...

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: When we first met, you asked me something.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You mentioned someone's name and asked if I knew it.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Oswald.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: He's my grandfather, although not by blood.
Dorothy springs to her feet.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: You...!

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Please sit. Causing a scene won't help anything.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: I'll explain.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: That would be wise.
Dorothy sits back down.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: I doubted you.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: I wasn't convinced that you were truly Dorothy from the Goddess Squad.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: I saw through your true intentions of either destroying or taking over the Ark early on.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: But I couldn't bring myself to dispose of you.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: According to my grandfather's records, you were the most radiant Goddess of Victory of all.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: My grandfather Oswald...

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: He allowed himself to be disgraced in order to protect you all.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: What... are you talking about?

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: After Operation Ark Guardian ended, the Ark deliberated over what to do with the Goddess Squad.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: They were certain you would wield influence far beyond the Central Government.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: So on the day you returned to the Ark, they mobilized every method they could.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: To bring you Goddesses down, and to drag you from your pedestal.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: No one adored the Goddess Squad more than my grandfather.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: He held a high enough position to oversee the entirety of Operation Ark Guardian.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: ... So he abandoned the Goddess Squad.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Because it was obvious to anyone that they would be destroyed if they returned to the Ark.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: You honestly expect me to believe that?

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: I know, there's no evidence of it.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: But back then, the Central Government was filled with the likes of Doban.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: If you're going to lie, you should at least get your stories straight.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: What you're saying contradicts Doban's account considerably.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Doban was lying.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Do you really expect me to believe you on your word alone?

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: There's nothing more I can say.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Doban lied to provoke you. That's all there is to it.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Then how did he know how Pinne died?

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: My grandfather apparently listened to every conversation in that temporary camp.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: He recorded it all in a book.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: ... He heard everything?

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: It seems he originally intended to wait longer, since moving too hastily could have exposed him.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: But after what happened to you, he moved up the schedule.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Because he feared the Goddesses would crumble.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Why didn't anyone say anything?

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: If what you're saying is true, why did he abandon us instead of telling the truth?

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Because even if he told you that entering the Ark meant you would be placed on trial, destroyed politically, and buried under false charges...

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You would still insist on coming to confirm it for yourselves.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: That was how deep your trust in the Ark ran after all.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: If he'd told you that there was a problem in the Ark and that he'd contact you later, you would never have left the Ark's entrance.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Because your concern for the Ark ran that deep.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: From my grandfather's perspective, he needed a lie that was convincingly realistic.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: A lie that would keep you away from the Ark.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Even if it bred hatred, rage, or a thirst for revenge.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Even if it meant you would one day return to exact that revenge.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: He wanted to make sure you never wished to set eyes on the Ark again.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Then why didn't he call us back afterward?

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: The Ark had long been dominated by V.T.C., and V.T.C. would never have tolerated your existence.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: There was nothing he could do, since they were too powerful.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: So my grandfather filed a false report saying the Goddess Squad had deserted.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Later, after V.T.C. was destroyed, the situation improved.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: But too much time had passed at that point, there was no way to find any of you.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Then that means you knew what we went through.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: You knew my true identity when I came to the Ark, so that means you knew of my objectives too.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Then why did you stay silent? Did you want to humiliate me?

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: As I said before, I doubted you.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: It was far too obvious that you had come to the Ark for revenge after being abandoned like that.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: So I kept watch this whole time.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: To determine whether you were the Dorothy of the past, or the Dorothy of the present, blinded by revenge.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: And I came to a conclusion.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Your grandfather would have been heartbroken to see what became of the Dorothy he once knew.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: But you know what? The only reason I'm this way is because of you...

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: I'm sorry.
Dorothy freezes.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: What... did you say?

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: I can't speak for the entire Ark, but I apologize.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: I... I didn't come here for an apology.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Dorothy.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: What do you want from the Ark?

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: I... The Ark...

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: I want to seize it... and get my revenge...

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You cannot.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: As I said, I reached a conclusion after observing you,

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: and my conclusion is this.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You won't act against the Ark.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: I could reduce the Ark to ruins right now if I wanted to!

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Perhaps. But you won't.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You had the power, the ability, the charisma, and yet you didn't.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You deliberately took the long way around.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You saved the Ark from the brink of ruin multiple times.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You were happy when Nikkes and people thanked you.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: As you said, you could have had your revenge at any moment you wanted. But you didn't act on it.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Watching you fail to fire a single shot at Doban was what convinced me.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You can't do it.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Because you are a Goddess.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: The Goddess of Victory.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: That's why you cannot do harm to the Ark.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: It's pitiful in a way.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You dreamed of revenge for such a long time, yet you soften immediately at the slightest recognition and respect.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: It's regrettable.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: And yet you cannot help but love Nikkes, humans, and humanity itself.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: It's truly sad.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: That you're destined only to be used by others, despite having the wherewithal to take revenge, yet unable to go through with it.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: How foolish of you.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Why you...! Who are you to talk to me like that?!

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: And that's precisely why...

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: You're still the Goddess of Victory.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: I can't leave you like this.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Tell me clearly. Are you an enemy or an ally?

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: If you are our enemy, we will strike you down.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: But if you are still our Goddess of Victory, the Ark will help you.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Without fail.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: We will help you become the Goddess of Victory once again. Humanity's hope. A true Goddess.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Please... stop. Don't say any more.
Because Dorothy feels like she might start to hope again.
Burningum places an old book on the table titled Dorothy.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: This is a handwritten record about you that my grandfather left behind.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: Read it. You deserve that much.
Burningum rises from his seat,
then turns and walks out.
He looks back at Dorothy staring blankly at the book on the table.
Burningum looks at Dorothy then straightens.
Dorothy lifts her head and looks back at Burningum.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: There was something I always wanted to say to you if I ever met you.
Burningum salutes.

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: For fighting on mankind's behalf...
"Please. Don't."
"Don't say it!"

lines.speaker: burningum
lines.text: ... I sincerely thank the Goddess Squad.
The door closes.
Dorothy stares ahead blankly.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: No...

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Ugh...

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: How... how could I have been so foolish?

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: So... easily...

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Ha... haha...
That evening...
Dorothy reads the book Burningum gave her.
The final page...
is filled with nothing but words of guilt toward the Goddesses,
which Dorothy stares at blankly through the entire night.
When morning comes,
she hears that a high-ranking official from the Central Government has requested a visit.
She doesn't want to go because it's certain to be an uncomfortable meeting.
Even so, she gets to her feet.
Dorothy sits in a chair in the visitation room.
Her visitor has yet to arrive.
But Dorothy is relieved as she still wrestles with her feelings.
A short while later, she hears the door opening behind her.
